instruction: Run `C:\Users\user\Desktop\active_filter.cir` in native PSpice. Keep the native simulator artifacts as `C:\Users\user\Desktop\active_filter.out`, `C:\Users\user\Desktop\active_filter_measure.txt`, and `C:\Users\user\Desktop\active_filter.dat`. The native run includes one baseline case and six single-parameter `+1%` perturbation cases. Based on the 1 kHz gain measurements, write `C:\Users\user\Desktop\sens.csv` with header `Component,Sensitivity,Relative`, listing all six perturbed components in descending `|Relative|`. For a perturbed component with baseline value `x0` and perturbed value `x1`, and baseline and perturbed gains `G0` and `G1` in dB, compute `Sensitivity = (G1 - G0) / (x1 - x0)` and `Relative = ((G1 - G0) / |G0|) / ((x1 - x0) / x0)`. [Software] Use the native PSpice command-line simulator `C:\Cadence\SPB_24.1\tools\bin\psp_cmd.exe`.
